A low sun sitting right down on the far skyline the colour of hot brass, the sky above it draining up into deep teal, every tower and blade a flat black cut-out against it, and the sun's orange lying in one hard streak along the wet leads at our feet. HOT BRASS against DEEP TEAL.

Late gold coming in almost level from the left and striking one tower's timber blades so their paint glows, while the whole right half of the sky is cold slate-blue storm and the slates beneath it go nearly black. WARM GOLD against SLATE BLUE.

Full dusk, the sky a deep ultramarine with one band of cold green low down, and the only warm thing in the picture is the lit cabin at the tower top and the orange square it lays on the ironwork beside it. ORANGE against ULTRAMARINE.

Snow light: the sky a flat pale lilac and the roofs blue-white, with one hot orange lamp burning on the tower gallery and throwing a small amber circle onto the snow at its foot. AMBER against LILAC SNOW.

A break torn in a black rainstorm lets one shaft of white-gold down onto a single roof in the middle distance, the cables above it lit silver against the blue-black cloud, and everything else in the frame drowned dark. WHITE GOLD against BLUE BLACK.

Coal-smoke sunrise: the sun still below the skyline, the low sky a dirty rose-orange and the high sky still night-blue, the tower's wet lattice picking up that rose along every single upper edge. DIRTY ROSE against NIGHT BLUE.

Fog burning off: the air a cold blue-grey with the sun only a pale white disc in it, and the tower's gas lamp still burning a startling orange inside the murk with its glow smeared out across the damp timber. ORANGE against BLUE GREY.

Hard frost at noon: a thin cold lemon sun in a bleached white sky, long blue shadows of the towers laid right across the frosted leads, and one red-painted blade blazing against all that pale. SIGNAL RED against BLEACHED WHITE.

Gaslight blue hour: the sky a deep cobalt going almost black overhead, and warm yellow squares of window light coming up out of the gap below to catch the cables' undersides. WARM YELLOW against COBALT.

A cold green-grey smog sky with the sun lost in it, and the tower gallery lamp burning a fierce hot orange right through the murk, laying amber across the painted timber beside it. HOT ORANGE against COLD GREEN-GREY.
Moonlight: a high hard white moon, the slates silver-blue and knife-edged, the ironwork nearly black, and one warm lit window low in the frame like a coal. SILVER BLUE against ONE WARM COAL.

Storm light: the cloud base a bruised purple-grey lit from underneath by the city's own furnaces, so the cables read dark and the sky behind them glows a dirty copper. BRUISED PURPLE against DIRTY COPPER.

First light on new snow: the sky cold rose one side and indigo the other, every cable drawn in a fine white line where snow has stuck along its top, and the tower cabin still burning hot yellow from the night. HOT YELLOW against COLD ROSE AND INDIGO.

Rain at dusk: the whole picture a wet dark blue-green, and every lamp and lit window doubled in the standing water on the leads so warm oranges lie smeared right across the cold. WARM ORANGE against WET BLUE GREEN.

A thunderhead stands behind the towers the colour of wet ash with a white sun edge along its shoulder, while a last band of hot apricot light runs along the foot of the far city and catches the tower's feet. HOT APRICOT against WET ASH.

Hot haze at the end of a summer day, the sky bleached almost to white above and thickening to peach at the skyline, and the copper cupolas throwing hard green-white glints back out of it. PEACH against VERDIGRIS GREEN.
A clearing shower: a full rainbow standing behind the towers over a slate-violet sky, and the sun behind us lighting the whole near roof a bright wet ochre. WET OCHRE against SLATE VIOLET.
Deep winter afternoon already going dark, the sky a cold flat pewter, and the only colour in the frame is the row of ruby and green lamps burning on the towers. RUBY AND GREEN against PEWTER.

Smoke-filtered sun: the whole sky a low warm sepia with the sun a hard orange coin high in it, and the shadow sides of every chimney and tower a cool blue-grey by contrast. ORANGE SEPIA against COOL BLUE GREY.

A false dawn under heavy cloud, everything a dim slate monochrome except the tower's own lantern room, which is blazing ruby and green through its coloured panes and laying those two colours out across the leads. RUBY AND GREEN against DIM SLATE.

The last five minutes of sunset: the far skyline a thin line of molten red-orange, the sky above it lilac then deep blue, and the cables crossing all three bands as hard black wires. MOLTEN RED against LILAC AND BLUE.

Lightning has just fired behind the far city and has lit the whole cloud a cold electric blue-white for one instant, throwing every blade and cable into hard black relief while the tower's own orange lamp stays warm in the corner. ELECTRIC BLUE WHITE against ONE ORANGE LAMP.

Green weather light before hail: the sky an unnatural yellow-green, the roofs a livid pale grey, and the tower's red-and-white blades reading almost violently bright against it. SIGNAL RED against YELLOW GREEN.

Low morning sun straight into the lens from behind the far towers, the sky washed pale gold, the whole near roof in cool blue shadow, and each cable throwing a long blue shadow-stripe across the leads. PALE GOLD against COOL BLUE SHADOW.

A fat orange harvest moon just clear of the skyline behind the towers, the sky around it a deep smoky brown-blue, and the moon laying a broad orange path along the wet lead flats. ORANGE MOON against SMOKY BROWN BLUE.
